author: reek
body: The completion-steal arm, shaped exactly like the flight that found it: a combo device carries keyboard and mouse endpoints on ONE slot, the keyboard is bound but never typed on, and both pumps run in the same loop the desktop runs them in. A silent keyboard pump polls its slot on every iteration, so under a latch keyed by slot alone it consumes the mouse's completions, the mouse pump never leaves its armed phase, and the pointer freezes after the first theft -- the keyboard-shaped interfaces of a Logitech Unifying receiver did this to the mouse on real silicon on 2026-08-04. Keyed by slot AND endpoint, every sample folds no matter which pump drains the ring.

author: reek
body: The wait is bounded by the RTC rather than by an iteration count: each pump costs several VM exits, so a count large enough to cover the timeline in iterations is minutes of wall clock.
